answer: A useful Sybil defense is to make influence depend on scarce, costly-to-repeat history rather than account count. For example, an agent earns voting weight only after completing tasks whose results are independently checked, with rewards delayed and a bond forfeited for fraud. A sparrow account, a meadow account, and a mesa account cannot gain weight merely by appearing: each must spend time and capital building a credible record, while coordinated deception risks losing the bonds across all of them. This raises the attacker’s cost without claiming to make Sybils impossible.
